metadata.note: Two Lehigh Valley passenger branches in the Finger Lakes, filling in gaps around the LV main line already on this map (lehigh_valley_railroad.geojson, which runs Sayre - Van Etten - Watkins Glen - east shore of Seneca Lake - Geneva and so misses Ithaca entirely by 23 km). FIRST, the Ithaca Branch: the Geneva and Ithaca Railroad was incorporated in 1870 and opened in 1873, connecting at Geneva with the New York Central's Auburn Road and at Ithaca with the Ithaca and Athens, which ran south to the Pennsylvania line near Sayre; the combined Geneva, Ithaca and Athens Railroad was acquired by the Lehigh Valley in 1876, giving it 75 miles from near Sayre to Geneva. An early timetable ran two passenger trains each way daily, the Express covering Ithaca-Geneva in 2 hours 5 minutes and the Accommodation in 3 hours, stopping at Pinckney, Ganoung, Taghanic, Trumansburg, Covert, Farmer, VanLiews, Ovid, Hayt's Corners and Romulus. SECOND, the Auburn and Ithaca Branch: the Cayuga Lake Railroad, financed by Henry Wells and Col. Edwin D. Morgan of Aurora, opened January 31 1873 and ran north out of Ithaca along the east bank of Cayuga Lake, reaching the New York Central at Cayuga Junction and later extending east to Auburn -- 42.2 miles Auburn to Ithaca. Sold after the financial crisis of 1873, it was part of the Lehigh Valley system by the end of that decade. The LV's locomotives famously wore 'Cornell red' for the university at on-line Ithaca. Passenger service on the Auburn and Ithaca Branch ended September 1 1948; ALL Lehigh Valley passenger service ended February 4 1961, when the last Maple Leaf, trains 7 and 8, ran through a blinding snowstorm. A THIRD branch has since been added here: the Hayts Corners, Ovid and Willard Railroad, a four-mile spur off the Geneva-Ithaca line opened 14 May 1883 to serve the Willard Asylum, which began with three passenger trains each way daily and was up to five by 1884.

geometry_sources: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap where the line survives (much of it is OSM's 'Ithaca Secondary', the ex-LV Sayre-Ithaca route), routed leg by leg through Sayre, Spencer, Ithaca, Trumansburg, Covert, Ovid, Hayts Corners, Romulus and Geneva. 76.3 mi against a documented 75 mi. MIXED QUALITY: 51.5 mi is real track; 23.2 mi across 3 legs are STRAIGHT-LINE APPROXIMATIONS where the grade is gone -- Ithaca-Trumansburg (9.4 mi); Hayts Corners-Romulus (2.9 mi); Romulus-Geneva (10.9 mi). The Ithaca-Trumansburg gap is expected: the track there was lifted in 1963. Straight legs are stitched to their traced neighbours' endpoints so the line stays continuous. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 20 m.

Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (partly OSM's named 'Auburn and Ithaca Branch'), routed through Auburn, Union Springs, Aurora, King Ferry, Ludlowville and Ithaca. 44.2 mi against a documented 42.2 mi. MIXED QUALITY: 34.7 mi is real track; one STRAIGHT-LINE APPROXIMATION of 8.7 mi covers King Ferry-Ludlowville, which is exactly the Aurora-Ludlowville stretch abandoned in 1950 and now absent from OSM. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 20 m.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: The date the Cayuga Lake Railroad's extension from Cayuga Junction east to Auburn opened is NOT sourced -- so the Auburn end of that feature may be drawn earlier than it existed; the 1879 handover to the Lehigh Valley is likewise approximate, the source saying only 'by the end of the decade'. Headways after the early two-trains-each-way timetable are estimates. The Ithaca station match is the weakest on both features at 2.4 km, because the LV's Ithaca terminal trackage is not cleanly represented in OSM. Whether local service on either branch outlasted the dates used here has not been checked. WILLARD BRANCH: the source gives both an official closing date of 30 June 1936 and an Ovid-Hayts Corners passenger end of 1937; the 1937 date is used here for the passenger feature and the conflict is left unresolved.

metadata.labelling: 2026-08-24: every feature in this file carries 'Lehigh Valley Railroad' at the start of its `line` field, which is what app.js shows in the hover tooltip, so LV routes are identifiable on the map without opening the data. Predecessor companies that were independent at the time are labelled '<Company> (Lehigh Valley predecessor)' rather than being relabelled as LV, because they were not yet Lehigh Valley in the years those features cover.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The Cayuga Lake Railroad opened January 31 1873, financed by Henry Wells -- of Wells Fargo, and of Wells College at Aurora -- and Col. Edwin D. Morgan. It ran north out of Ithaca along the east bank of Cayuga Lake to meet the New York Central at Cayuga Junction, and was later extended east to Auburn. CAVEAT: the date of that Auburn extension is not sourced, so the Auburn end may be drawn before it opened. Sold after the financial crisis of 1873. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
